headline: New Hampshire 1st District candidates split over how to lower costs
dek: At a Meredith forum, Republican Anthony DiLorenzo and Democrat Stefany Shaheen agreed housing and energy are hurting families but offered sharply different federal remedies.
body: Republican Anthony DiLorenzo and Democrat Stefany Shaheen used a Meredith forum Tuesday to present competing answers to one of New Hampshire’s most persistent political questions: how can families afford housing, heat and everyday necessities? The two candidates are running for the U.S. House seat in the 1st Congressional District, and the event came less than a month before the Nov. 3 general election. The forum was hosted by New Hampshire Public Radio, The Laconia Daily Sun and the Granite State News Collaborative at Twin Barns Brewing Company.

The candidates agreed that affordability is a serious problem, but they described its causes in opposite terms. DiLorenzo, a Seacoast businessman and Republican nominee, blamed what he called federal fiscal mismanagement under the Biden administration and argued that his experience building businesses would help him push wages higher. Shaheen, the Democratic nominee, pointed instead to President Donald Trump’s policies, including tariffs on Canada and the war with Iran, which she said are raising costs for New Hampshire households and small businesses. These were campaign arguments, not independent findings; [NHPR’s account of the forum](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2026-10-07/cost-of-living-nh-newhampshire-1st-congressional-district-2026) attributes them to the candidates.

Energy policy produced one of the clearest contrasts. Shaheen said the conflict with Iran has pushed up gasoline and heating-oil costs and argued that Congress should expand the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program. She said heating oil prices for New Hampshire families had risen by nearly half this winter, a figure presented during the forum rather than a new state price report. DiLorenzo said high Northeast energy costs reflect federal policy choices and proposed pursuing a natural-gas pipeline from Pennsylvania while expanding nuclear power. His campaign’s [issues page](https://dilorenzoforcongress.com/issues/) describes a broader goal of energy independence using multiple sources without subsidies, while Shaheen’s [campaign platform](https://stefanyshaheen.com/priorities/) emphasizes local clean generation, grid upgrades and efficiency.

Housing was another area of agreement without agreement on the mechanism. DiLorenzo proposed a federal program modeled on the Small Business Administration that would make financing available to first-time and moderate-income buyers. He also said he would work with New Hampshire’s state leaders on affordability. Shaheen called for limiting private-equity purchases of single-family homes and expanding tax credits to encourage permanently affordable housing. Her campaign platform separately calls for more first-time-buyer assistance and for using public buildings and land for housing, but those are campaign proposals, not enacted programs.

The candidates also connected household costs to immigration and trade. Shaheen said the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement need stricter accountability, including body cameras, limits on agents wearing masks and a focus on deporting people convicted of violent crimes. DiLorenzo said he supports enforcing immigration law while pursuing reforms and argued that employers are struggling to find workers. He also criticized tariffs and said reducing trade barriers could help domestic manufacturing. Neither candidate offered a detailed cost estimate for the policies discussed, and the forum did not resolve how Congress would pay for their proposals.

Foreign policy entered the affordability debate when moderators asked about U.S. military action against Iran. DiLorenzo said the United States should end the war and bring troops home, while arguing that the campaign had reduced Iran’s ability to build nuclear weapons. Shaheen also called for an end to the conflict, but focused on its effect on fuel prices and said the United States should not prolong the fighting. [NHPR’s full forum recording and summary](https://www.nhpr.org/politics/2026-10-06/1st-district-newhampshire-congress-dilorenzo-shaheen-live-debate-youtube) provide the candidates’ longer answers and show that both framed the issue as part of the economic pressure facing New Hampshire residents.

The race matters locally because the winner will represent a district where housing costs, heating bills and access to workers are immediate concerns, while having limited control over the federal policies the candidates debated. The forum gave voters a side-by-side comparison: DiLorenzo offered business growth, pipeline construction and a buyer-financing program; Shaheen emphasized tariff changes, energy assistance, clean-energy investment and restrictions on large housing investors. The practical test for either agenda would come after legislation, appropriations and agency rules, not simply after a campaign promise.

The Meredith event was part of a series of New Hampshire candidate forums planned for October. The [Laconia Daily Sun’s event notice](https://www.laconiadailysun.com/news/local/voters-to-hear-from-dilorenzo-shaheen-at-congressional-candidate-forum-tuesday/article_2b423db2-d5b3-4b35-8545-9b6c7a604e73.html) said the partnership would continue with forums for the 2nd Congressional District, governor and U.S. Senate races. For the 1st District candidates, the next phase is translating broad promises about affordability into specific votes, budgets and programs before Election Day.
location: Twin Barns Brewing Company, Meredith, New Hampshire
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: New Hampshire 1st District candidates debate costs | NorthEast News
seoDescription: Anthony DiLorenzo and Stefany Shaheen offered different plans on housing, heating costs, energy and immigration at a New Hampshire 1st District forum.
